chapter: Return to Atlanta and move north
title: Slim and Shorty's routines and a Sweet Sue demonstration
summary: Green recalls their numbers (Sweet Sue, Broadway Melody, Bugle Call Rag as the encore) and demonstrates Sweet Sue with humming and taps.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: So anyhow, we went out there, and Shorty and Slim, you know, and we did our "Sweet Sue" and the "Broadway Melody", and we really had to do an encore, which was the "Bugle Call Rag", you know. That's where we had a lot of pleasure.
What was the "Sweet Sue" like?
It was a song, famous song.
How did it go?
Da-da-dee-dunk-dah-dah, da-da-dunk-dah-dah, Sweet Sue, yes, you, you know, like that.
And what were the taps like in that?
Well, I mean we was -- we had routines. We had a routine we was doing.
You were doing, what sort of tapping were you doing?
Well, it was just what they call the authentic tap dancing, you know, regular, standard tap dancing, see.
Was it sort of fast?
No --
Can you show me just --
Yeah, well, I could show you, but -- sure.
(Recording interruption)
So in order to give you a better idea of what it was, we did the "Sweet Sue" and "Broadway Melody" and the "Bugle Call Rag". Now, to give you a better idea of what

it was, I shall try to demonstrate a bit of 'Sweet Sue' and tap dancing. All right? I think we'll go now, so I'll sing the melody, or hum the melody where you can get an idea how it went with the tap dancing. All right, here we go.
(Tape Five)
This is tape number four -- tape number five. We're about to begin.
Now we're in the 'Sweet Sue', the melody, tap dancing, here we go.
(Humming, singing and tap dancing interlude)
